input.doc_title: Graph-Aware Prompting for Reliable Section Generation
input.doc_summary: We present a graph-guided prompting workflow for long-form scientific writing that prioritizes evidence and citation consistency. Our method constructs a document graph that encodes section dependencies and uses strict JSON schemas and evidence-aware prompts to generate and validate individual sections. At generation time, the system (1) builds a section graph and schedules leaf-first writing, (2) retrieves and injects relevant evidence for each section, (3) produces JSON-constrained section outputs, and (4) assembles a LaTeX manuscript with refs.bib. We evaluate the approach by comparing it to a baseline linear prompting pipeline on two topical domains, measuring citation coverage, hallucination rate, and reviewer-style scores. Results show improved citation coverage and reduced unsupported assertions while keeping edits and post-hoc audits straightforward via machine-readable outputs. We intentionally state conservative claims and require explicit source citations for all factual assertions. The paper contributes practical artifacts: a graph-based section scheduler, an evidence-injection protocol per section, and an audit-friendly JSON output format that integrates with standard LaTeX/bib workflows. Our experiments use internal notes and a small curated PDF set where available; metrics focus on citation fidelity and factual consistency rather than broad generalization.
input.target_audience: ACL Workshop on Natural Language Generation
input.parent_summary: Detail the graph construction (section graph and dependencies), the JSON schema for section outputs, evidence retrieval and ranking, evidence-aware prompt templates, leaf-first generation and assembly rules, and the LaTeX + refs.bib assembly process. Include conservative validation checks and failure modes.

output.title: Section graph construction and scheduling
output.summary: Describe construction of the document section graph, node and edge semantics (section dependencies, prerequisite relations), graph serialization, and the leaf-first scheduling algorithm used to order section generation.

output.title: JSON schema for section outputs
output.summary: Specify the strict JSON schema for each generated section (fields, types, required citation/evidence fields, machine-checkable constraints), validation procedure, and how JSON outputs facilitate edits and audits.

output.title: Evidence retrieval, ranking, and injection protocol
output.summary: Detail the retrieval sources and indexing, query formulation, ranking/scoring of candidate evidence, selection thresholds, and the protocol for injecting ranked evidence into section prompts.

output.title: Evidence-aware prompt templates and JSON-constrained generation
output.summary: Present the prompt template families that enforce citation-first writing, instruct JSON-constrained outputs, include evidence citation anchors, and describe iterative generation/validation loops for a single section.

output.title: Assembly into LaTeX + refs.bib, validation checks, and failure modes
output.summary: Explain rules for assembling JSON sections into a LaTeX manuscript with refs.bib, conservative validation checks (citation coverage, unsupported-claim detection), logging, and documented failure modes and remediation steps.
